function: Learned MLP surrogate of the map from BSW amplitudes to RIS radiation pattern, used by simulated annealing to configure beams and nulls maximizing SLNR (p. 2, 6, 9).
system: Single-antenna Tx and K single-antenna Rxs; 100-element single-row reflecting wave-controlled RIS with varactors, 25 BSWs; narrowband LoS far-field; 2.45 GHz (p. 5, 7).
method: Supervised MLP regression (TensorFlow Keras), architecture tuned by genetic algorithm; simulated annealing optimizes BSW amplitudes through the trained NN; lookup-table initialization (p. 6-9, 11-12).
data_channel: Own MATLAB simulation: 100,000 random BSW-amplitude and radiation-pattern pairs; LoS steering-vector channels at normal incidence; no 3GPP model, public dataset, or measurement (p. 5, 7).
test_conditions: Train 90,000, validate 10,000 random samples, one RIS and channel; SA tested at trained angles (Table 2) and interpolated angles (Table 3) (p. 8, 10-11).
baselines: SA on the exact simulated system with direct Rx feedback; SA from zero start versus lookup-table start; no earlier learned method compared (p. 10-12).
metrics: NN training and validation MSE (7.4851e-4, 8.4779e-4); SLNR in dB after SA convergence, mean, min, max, standard deviation; radiation patterns (p. 8, 10-12).
q1_support: p. 5: "where all channels are narrowband line-of-sight (LoS), flat-fading" - custom MATLAB simulator with steering-vector channels (p. 7); no 3GPP TR 38.901, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 10: "only involve angles on which the MLP was trained" - Table 3 (p. 11) then uses off-grid directions by linear interpolation of the NN outputs, with the same RIS, channel, and band; read as a held-out part of the same data, not a new scenario. No other condition is varied.
q3_support: p. 10: "against the performance of SA executed in the deterministic simulation" - the only reference is non-learned (SA on the exact model); no earlier learned method or standard learned architecture is compared (the DNN of [12] is only discussed on p. 2).
q4_support: p. 9: "it is not computationally intensive" - qualitative remark on SA only; no complexity order, FLOPs, parameter count (Fig. 8 shows layer widths only), or runtime is reported.
q5_support: p. 7: "a dataset was generated with Nmax = 100,000 pairs of data arrays" - own simulated data with no code or data link and no public dataset; TensorFlow [43] is the library only.
notes: Borderline no_learning, included: the MLP is a learned surrogate of the RIS response (p. 2: "we will turn to the use of machine learning (ML) tools to solve the RIS configuration problem") while the non-learned SA searches the configuration; reviewer to confirm that a learned surrogate counts as performing the function. Borderline q2: the nearest candidate is Table 3 (off-grid angles by interpolation, p. 11); Fig. 11 changes N from 25 to 50 and Fig. 10 uses a 3.5 V BSW, but neither is reported as a test of the trained NN. Hardware design of the wave-controlled RIS comes from earlier work [5], so the function is not metasurface hardware design.
